one_line: A 74-second 3D Pixar-style AI cartoon where a messy toddler is scolded, runs away to a village, and is reunited with tearful parents.

hook.visual: Smiling toddler in a red T-shirt sits in a puddle of spilled chocolate on a wooden floor, hands and face smeared; a woman peeks in from the open door at the left edge of the frame (0.0 s).
hook.on_screen_text: none (no title card or captions in any sampled frame)
hook.first_spoken_line: You made a huge mess! Look at this mess on the floor! (Whisper, 0.0 to 5.0 s)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Observed: a close, bright, glossy toddler face at 0.0 s, then within 4 s an angry father runs in and points a finger while the mother covers her mouth. Inferred: the scolding of a small child is an instant emotional and parenting trigger that needs no setup.

beats.observed: Toddler laughing in the chocolate spill (0.0 s); angry father in a blue shirt runs in, mother in a green top covers her mouth (2.0 s); father leans over and points a finger while the toddler looks up (4.0 s).
beats.spoken: 'You made a huge mess! Look at this mess on the floor!' (Whisper, 0.0 to 5.04 s)

beats.observed: Two extreme close-ups of the toddler's face at 6.0 and 8.0 s: wide green eyes, tears running down chocolate-smeared cheeks, mouth quivering.

Night bedroom with a moon and stars: toddler sleeping between both parents (10.0 s) under a thought bubble showing the father pointing at him over a chocolate cake (12.0 to 14.0 s); he frowns, then wakes crying at 16.0 s and is in tight close-up at 18.0 s.

Barefoot child, now looking older and walking, trudges alone down a muddy village road in rain (20.0 s); a dark car passes and splashes him (22.0 s); sad close-up (24.0 s); close-up of a bare muddy foot in a puddle (26.0 s).
Crying child in a village market with goats (28.0 to 30.0 s); an elderly woman and then an elderly man appear; the man crouches and pats his head (34.0 to 36.0 s).
beats.spoken: 'Uncle, I need job, please!' (30.0 to 34.0 s) and 'Oh, okay, okay, little one.' (34.0 to 37.0 s) (Whisper, timestamps rounded to whole seconds)

beats.observed: Back in a modern living room, the mother in a green cardigan points at the father, who sits on the floor crying and clutching a white baby onesie (38.0 to 44.0 s). Then the father drives, anxious, with the mother beside him (46.0 to 48.0 s) into a village (50.0 s).
beats.spoken: 'You should not have fought with our child!' (37.0 to 40.0 s). 'The child left the house because of you!' (40.0 to 43.0 s). 'Where could he be?' (47.0 to 49.0 s)

beats.observed: Grey car stops in a crowded goat-filled village street (52.0 to 54.0 s); a small plate reads roughly 'LK 2326' [unclear]; a man in a beige tunic and a woman in green speak to villagers (56.0 s); close-up of a small bare, muddy foot on straw (58.0 s).
beats.spoken: 'Have you seen a little boy?' (54.0 to 56.0 s)

beats.observed: Man in a village tunic gasps, then smiles through tears (60.0 to 64.0 s); he and a woman in an apron kneel and hug a small black-haired toddler in torn clothes (66.0 s); close-ups of the family hugging and the toddler laughing through tears (68.0 to 72.0 s).

payoff: Parents hug the lost toddler and he laughs through tears, from about 1:06 to the end at 1:14 (the last 8 s of 74).
cta: Description: 'Don't forget to Like, Share, and Subscribe for more emotional animated stories!' No on-screen CTA.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: the moral is stated in the description ('Never Scold Your Child', 'patience, love, and care'), which gives a parent a reason to send it to a partner or relative. Only 15 comments on 539,455 views, so discussion is low and the engagement is mostly passive likes.
why_it_worked: 539,455 views is 245x the account's median of 2,200 (meta.json), so this is a rare breakout on a small account. Inferred: the title 'Never Scold Your Child' and the emotional arc fit what Shorts or YouTube recommends to parents and children.

Observed: the open loop 'where is the boy' opens when the child walks away alone (about 20 s), is voiced at 47 s ('Where could he be?') and only closes at the 66 s reunion, so the payoff is held back until roughly the last 8 s.
4,737 likes at 0.88% is solid for a 74 s video, but 15 comments on 539K views shows low active reaction. Inferred: much passive viewing.
paid_signal: no, inferred: like_rate 0.88% is above the 0.3% paid-pattern line and nothing in frames or caption suggests promotion. The very low comment count (15) is odd but not proof of anything.

solo_route.how: 1) Write a 20 to 30 s Hebrew micro-story with 8 to 10 shots and 3 spoken lines, e.g. kid spills chocolate, parent reacts, kid is hiding, parent says sorry, they hug. 2) Take LumeBook's own illustration of a child hero and use it as the reference/first frame for EVERY shot, so the hero stays the same child; this video fails exactly here. 3) Generate each shot as image-to-video clips of 3 to 5 s and cut them in CapCut. 4) Add an AI Hebrew voice for the 2 to 3 lines plus soft music, and put burned-in Hebrew captions under each line. Generate extra takes for the face close-ups. Expect 3 to 5 hours for 25 s.
solo_route.needs: Nothing external. Avoid real children's photos for the hero. Do not use the word Pixar in titles, hashtags or prompts (brand and trademark risk). Add the platform AI label. Do not use an AI voice cloned from a real person.

lumebook_version.hook_he: שוקולד על הרצפה ואבא בדלת. מה עושים?
lumebook_version.concept: A 20 to 30 s AI story starring one consistent LumeBook illustrated hero in LumeBook's own 3D-illustrated look, where the spilled-chocolate moment ends with the parent laughing and hugging instead of scolding, then cuts to the hero on a LumeBook book cover.

evidence_notes: Observed AI cues: glossy, plastic-looking skin with uniformly rosy cheeks and glassy tear drops; hair rendered as clean, repeated strands; hands in the sampled frames look mostly plausible with no obvious extra fingers, but sampling was every 2 s, so morphing between frames cannot be ruled out. Strong continuity failures: the toddler's eyes read green at 0.0 s and blue at 20.0 s; he looks about 1 year old at 0.0 s and 3 to 4 years old and walking at 20.0 s; his shorts change from white to beige. The parents look different in the home scenes (blue-shirt brown-haired father, ponytailed mother in green) and the village scenes (dark-haired father in a tunic, short-haired mother in an apron). The final reunion is with a black-haired toddler in torn clothes, not the blonde boy in the red T-shirt. Inferred: each shot was generated without a character reference. The car badge at 54.0 s is a distorted logo and the plate is only roughly legible ('LK 2326' [unclear]). Tool: the description says 'This video contains AI-generated visuals and animation created using advanced generative AI tools' and names no product, and the caption says '3D Pixar Animation'. I cannot tell which tool made it. Transcript: Whisper has speech only at 0 to 5 s and then 30 to 74 s, with sound tags such as [GASP] and [GIGGLES]; timestamps are rounded to whole seconds from 30 s, so treat timing as approximate. The line 'Uncle, I need job, please!' cannot be matched to a visible mouth. Whether the 5 to 30 s gap is silence or music I cannot tell. made_by brand_inhouse means only the account's own upload. Likeness and consent: no real person or celebrity look-alike is visible; but the film depicts a crying, scolded toddler and parent blame, which would be a bad fit if a real child's photo were used, and the 'Pixar' style name is a brand risk. Do not use real customer child photos for this kind of distress story.
